metadata.title: Apple Turned $1,000 Into $2.6 Million. The Next Trillion Gets Harder

content.text:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
Apple Inc. (AAPL, Financials) has produced the kind of return that investors seldom enjoy twice. A $1,000 investment in Apple when it went public in December 1980 would be worth about $2.6 million now. That background makes what follows complicated.Apple has a far wider basis to work from in delivering its next stretch of growth, with the business worth around $4.61 trillion. That adds even more pressure to Wednesday's product event.It will be the first major gadget lineup under CEO John Ternus, and is believed to feature Apple's first foldable iPhone. A new form factor is relevant to investors if it can do more than inspire launch-day enthusiasm.Apple requires upgradeable devices and products that can defend their premium pricing and lock people into its broader ecosystem.One recent forecast has Apple growing about 9.4% a year through fiscal 2031. If its valuation and share count are similar, at that pace its market worth might potentially exceed $6 trillion. Apple has already produced spectacular profits. The bigger question is what will power the next step.Investors want to see signs during Wednesday's debut that Apple still has the ability to make goods that can move the needle at a $4.61 trillion company.
